free_tier.stated: no free tier of any kind. Every plan is paid: 'Chat $25/mo', 'Developer from $50/mo', 'Business Custom'. The Chat plan advertises 'Flat-rate pricing designed for scale with unlimited tokens' across a catalogue of '40,000+ open models', capped at a 32K context window and 4 concurrent units.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: USD 25 a month for unlimited interactive chat tokens is the cheapest per-token cost in evaluated offerings if the workload is a single interactive chat; it buys nothing for an agent, because the Chat plan excludes API traffic and automation.

limits.value: on the cheapest plan the context window and 4 concurrent units bind before anything else: 32K of context and four units in flight, with no production API on that tier at all.

evidence.proved: the plan table's three columns are 'Chat $25/mo', 'Developer from $50/mo', 'Business Custom' with no free column; 'Credits expire: Never'; 'Token volume: Unlimited' on Chat and Business; 'Concurrent units: 4' on Chat, 100 on Developer, quoted

'Flat-rate pricing designed for scale with unlimited tokens'; 'Chat plan is for interactive, human-driven use by the purchaser. Not for reselling, app/API traffic, background automation, or benchmarking', quoted

record.notes: The word 'unlimited' is the trap: the same page's footnote restricts the Chat plan to human-driven use and excludes benchmarking, and the Developer plan is metered per token instead. So the free-looking offer is neither free nor unlimited for a programmatic workload. No free trial is published, which makes this a paid-only record rather than trial-only.
